sources.title: Human History Map, historical-basemap civilization index
sources.note: Primary project data checked for exact IDs, labels, aliases, start/end fields and geometry intervals. Local GeoJSON was also point-tested; the public cards disclose material omissions and do not treat simplified shapes as legal borders.

sources.title: U.S. Office of the Historian, A Guide to the United States’ History of Recognition, Diplomatic, and Consular Relations, by Country, since 1776: Yemen
sources.note: Official diplomatic history checked for British Aden, northern and southern recognition dates, the 1970 southern name change and 22 May 1990 unification. Its broad post-1918 wording is not used to erase the northern imamate/kingdom.

sources.title: United Nations Treaty Collection, Agreement on the establishment of the Republic of Yemen
sources.note: Official treaty record checked for the Sana’a signature on 22 April 1990, entry into force on 22 May 1990, parties and authentic Arabic text.

sources.title: United Nations Treaty Collection, Historical Information: Yemen
sources.note: Official UN succession record checked for the 22 May 1990 merger, the Republic of Yemen name, Sana’a capital, single UN membership and continuity of earlier treaty obligations.

sources.title: United Nations, Yemen member-state profile
sources.note: Official UN member-state page checked for the 22 May 1990 merger of Democratic Yemen and Yemen into one Member named Yemen. Used for legal continuity only, not a claim of unified de facto control.

sources.title: United Nations Police, United Nations Yemen Observation Mission background
sources.note: Official UN mission history checked for the September 1962 northern civil war, external involvement and UN observation mission.

sources.title: UN Human Rights Council, Situation of human rights in Yemen, including violations and abuses since September 2014, A/HRC/42/CRP.1
sources.note: Original UN report checked at paragraphs 93 to 110 for the 1990 transition, 1993 election, 1994 war and failed secession, postwar centralization, 2014 Houthi takeover and 2015 intervention.

sources.title: United Nations Department of Political and Peacebuilding Affairs, Yemen
sources.note: Official conflict timeline checked for the National Dialogue, September 2014 seizure of Sana’a, 26 March 2015 coalition intervention and continuing UN mediation.

sources.title: World Bank, IDA to IFC Agribusiness Program Phase 1 for Yemen: concept-stage Project Information Document, 22 January 2026
sources.note: Original project document checked at page 2 for rival Sana’a- and Aden-based authorities, duplicated institutions and currencies, damaged infrastructure and the preparation date. Used as a dated description, not a border-recognition source.

sources.title: United Nations in Yemen, statement on removal of UN equipment and assets, 30 January 2026
sources.note: Official dated statement checked for the terms “Houthi de facto authorities” in Sana’a-controlled areas and “Internationally Recognised Government” for Marib. It does not define a permanent frontier.

sources.title: WHO Yemen, WHO scales up health response as escalating conflict deepens health needs, 24 September 2026
sources.note: Official WHO update checked for its publication date, assessed-facility functionality, trauma-capacity and displacement figures. Point-in-time emergency figures are dated in the card.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Old City of Sana’a
sources.note: Official World Heritage entry checked for highland setting, tower houses, bustans, local building materials, urban history and threats. Heritage facts describe the old city, not every Yemeni home.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Old Walled City of Shibam
sources.note: Official entry checked for mud-brick towers up to seven storeys, defensive planning, flood agriculture and drainage/sanitation pressures. “Skyscraper city” is explanatory shorthand.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Historic Town of Zabid
sources.note: Official entry checked for courtyard houses, souq, canal pattern, mosques, madrasas and the historic university. Medieval prestige is treated as antecedent heritage, not an achievement of the modern republic.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Socotra Archipelago
sources.note: Official World Heritage entry checked for plant-species and endemism figures, island geography and conservation value. The card distinguishes ancient biodiversity from a modern political achievement.

sources.title: UNDP Yemen, solar project cuts cost of energy by 65 per cent and earns Ashden Award, 2 July 2020
sources.note: Original UNDP report checked for three frontline communities, women and youth trained as technicians and microgrid managers, donor role and reported local cost reduction. It is a small programme, not national electrification.

sources.title: UNICEF Yemen, Providing a safe learning space for children in Yemen, 7 May 2025
sources.note: Original field story checked for the Jader community school, earlier one-hour walk and road danger, community action and UNICEF’s 3.7 million out-of-school estimate. One village is not treated as nationally typical.

sources.title: UNICEF Yemen, How the rehabilitation of school toilets is boosting learning for children, 26 March 2018
sources.note: Original child-centred field report checked for Mohamed carrying drinking water, lack of privacy and running water, effects on girls and rehabilitation of WASH facilities in 232 schools in 2017.

sources.title: UNICEF Yemen, Improving WASH, sanitation and hygiene through education, 1 February 2024
sources.note: Original programme account checked for 6,448 children in 20 Lahj schools learning about handwashing, open defecation, open wells and cholera prevention. Scope and place are retained.

sources.title: UNICEF Yemen, Emergency latrines: Restoring health and dignity to Yemen’s most vulnerable populations
sources.note: Original Al Jawf displacement-camp story checked for donkey water collection, open defecation, missed classes and the privacy and cleanliness provided by emergency latrines and water points.

sources.title: UNICEF Yemen, A community midwife saving lives as conflict rages
sources.note: Original field story checked for Warda’s remote Marib work, antenatal and postnatal care, referrals, health education and family-planning counselling. One midwife illustrates a service model rather than national coverage.

sources.title: UNICEF Yemen, Health, hope and the hard road ahead, 4 August 2025
sources.note: Original clinic story checked for vaccinations, vitamins, fever care and delivery of 288 primary-health-care kits in late 2024 and early 2025. Programme support is distinguished from a fully functioning national system.

sources.title: WHO Yemen, Restoring immunity by reaching every child, 16 March 2026
sources.note: Official WHO update checked for southern interruption of circulating vaccine-derived poliovirus type 2, staff training and surveillance. The geographic limitation is explicit; no nationwide eradication claim is made.

sources.title: Government of Uzbekistan, History of Uzbekistan
sources.note: Official national account checked for formation of the Uzbek Soviet Socialist Republic in 1924, Tashkent becoming capital in 1930 and the 1991 independence date. Political praise and unsourced performance claims are not adopted.

sources.title: Government of Uzbekistan, 31 August ,  Day of Proclamation of the State Independence of the Republic of Uzbekistan
sources.note: Official Uzbek-language commemoration checked for the Supreme Soviet declaration and constitutional independence law on 31 August 1991, renaming of the republic and 1 September holiday. Ceremonial language is omitted.

sources.title: United Nations in Uzbekistan, About the United Nations in Uzbekistan
sources.note: Official UN country page checked for admission on 2 March 1992 and later UN presence. Membership is used as a statehood marker, not as a judgment about government performance.

sources.title: OSCE ODIHR, Republic of Uzbekistan early presidential election, 4 December 2016: final report
sources.note: Original observer report checked for Karimov’s September 2016 death, Mirziyoyev’s interim appointment and election, the 25-year presidency and concentrated powers. Observer judgments are attributed and dated.

sources.title: President of Uzbekistan, Shavkat Mirziyoyev takes office as President, 14 December 2016
sources.note: Official account checked for the 4 December 2016 election and 14 December inauguration. It confirms sequence only; its political evaluations are not treated as independent findings.

sources.title: World Bank, Uzbekistan: Reforms for a Sustainable Transformation toward a Market Economy
sources.note: Original programme document checked for post-2017 foreign-exchange, price, enterprise and social-protection reforms and World Bank financing. Reforms are described as a process with costs and unfinished work.

sources.title: OSCE ODIHR, Republic of Uzbekistan parliamentary elections, 27 October 2024: final report
sources.note: Original observer report checked for the election date, recent legal changes, constrained political environment, absence of genuine choice and procedural concerns. These are attributed findings, not timeless labels.

sources.title: Constitution of the Republic of Uzbekistan, official Uzbek text, 2023 edition
sources.note: Original official text checked for Article 4’s exact Latin-script Uzbek sentence naming Uzbek as the state language. The card translates it plainly and notes that the constitution also respects other languages and traditions.

sources.title: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage, Palov culture and tradition
sources.note: Official nomination entry checked for ingredients, hospitality, weddings, New Year, memorial meals, charity and intergenerational teaching. It records a living tradition without implying every meal or household is identical.

sources.title: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage, Askiya, the art of wit
sources.note: Official entry checked for improvised verbal duels, family and community celebrations, performance conventions and social commentary. The entry’s historically male practitioner base is stated rather than generalized away.

sources.title: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage, Khorazm dance, Lazgi
sources.note: Official entry checked for themes, music, community and family occasions and audience participation. It is presented as a Khorazm tradition within Uzbekistan, not a universal national routine.

sources.title: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage, Margilan Crafts Development Centre safeguarding atlas and adras making
sources.note: Official best-practice entry checked for the 2007 centre, natural-material ikat production, master-apprentice teaching, community role and earlier threats to transmission.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Samarkand ,  Crossroad of Cultures
sources.note: Official entry checked for the city’s long history, Timurid monuments, courtyards and gardens and Ulugh Beg’s observatory. Pre-1991 heritage is explicitly labeled antecedent history.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Astronomy and World Heritage thematic study
sources.note: Original UNESCO/IAU study checked for the fifteenth-century Samarkand observatory, large sextant and collaborative star-table and trigonometric work. The achievement belongs to Ulugh Beg’s scholarly court, not the modern republic.

sources.title: NASA Earth Observatory, Archaeology from Afar in Uzbekistan
sources.note: Original NASA account checked for use of CORONA, ASTER, Landsat and commercial images since 2008, dozens of candidate sites and follow-up fieldwork. Remote sensing assists discovery; it does not replace excavation.

sources.title: World Bank, Greening the desert: landscape restoration in Uzbekistan’s battle against sand and dust storms, 4 December 2024
sources.note: Original World Bank feature checked for Soviet irrigation-driven Aral shrinkage, the roughly 60,000-square-kilometre Aralkum seabed and present restoration work. It does not claim the Aral Sea has been restored.

sources.title: World Bank, Climate and Environment Program in Central Asia, 29 June 2025
sources.note: Official programme brief checked for the reported 500,000 hectares of degraded land under afforestation in Uzbekistan and the multinational/donor context. The figure concerns treatment, not ecological recovery of the whole Aral basin.

sources.title: UNICEF Uzbekistan, Water, sanitation and hygiene
sources.note: Official programme page checked for 2021 to 2022 MICS household indicators, on-premises water and handwashing gaps, school disparities and improvements in selected Karakalpakstan schools and health facilities.

sources.title: UNICEF Uzbekistan, Inclusive education through the eyes of children, 2 June 2026
sources.note: Official release checked for the children’s exhibition, estimated number of children with disabilities, low mainstream enrolment and 50 model schools. Estimates and programme scope are retained.

sources.title: UNICEF Uzbekistan, A father’s journey: Bakhriddin Choriev’s dedication to supporting children with disabilities, 17 February 2025
sources.note: Original family story checked for the father’s move, daily school support and advocacy. It illustrates one family’s choices and the burden of inaccessible services, not a prescribed family model.

sources.title: WHO Europe, A lifelong commitment to ensuring children receive the care and protection they deserve, 22 April 2024
sources.note: Original WHO profile checked for paediatric nurse Umida’s vaccination-room work since 1993, counselling of families and current primary-care setting. One professional is not treated as proof of universal access.

sources.title: WHO Europe, Uzbekistan moves to improve medicine affordability at primary health care level, 26 November 2024
sources.note: Official WHO account checked for the Syrdarya reimbursement pilot, subsequent legislation and the planned 2027 nationwide system. The card distinguishes completed pilot work from a future target.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Keep exact indexed ID yemen-1920, label Yemen / alias Republic of Yemen, circa 1920 to open. Distinct earlier same-name IDs are yemen (1000 to 1530) and yemen-1715 (1715 to 1878); do not alias or overwrite them. Eight geometries cover 1920 to 1930, 1930 to 1938, 1938 to 1945, 1945 to 1960, 1960 to 1994, 1994 to 2000, 2000 to 2010 and 2010 to 2020; none covers after 2020. The 1920 to 1938 polygon excludes Sana’a, Taiz, Saada, Aden and Socotra while including Mukalla; 1945+ shapes include Sana’a, Taiz, Saada and Mukalla but still exclude Aden and Socotra. Public caveat states the record compresses a northern imamate/kingdom, two republics after 1967 and the 1990 Republic, and that present de facto control is dated rather than treated as a legal partition.

Keep exact indexed ID uzbekistan, label Uzbekistan / alias Republic of Uzbekistan, circa 1994 to open. The modern state declared independence on 31 August 1991; the Uzbek SSR formed in 1924 is an antecedent, not this independent identity. Three geometries cover 1994 to 2000, 2000 to 2010 and 2010 to 2020, leaving a 1991 to 1994 gap and no post-2020 geometry. Shapes include Tashkent, Samarkand, Nukus and Ferghana, leave Termez just outside, and extend too far north/west; public caveat says they are simplified navigation shapes, not legal boundaries. No invented fall or successor.
